name: federated_communities
description: One row per API version a community offers. A community that speaks 1_0 and 1_1 has two rows here and one row in communities.

columns.name: remote
columns.note: Renamed for the same reason as communities.remote: legacy's `foreign` is a reserved word in PostgreSQL and unparseable unquoted in SQLite.

columns.name: public_key
columns.description: The community this endpoint belongs to. Joined by key, not by id.

columns.name: api_version
columns.description: '1_0' or '1_1'. Selects which route set the endpoint serves — see server/federation/.

columns.name: end_point
columns.description: Base URL. The federation client appends the api_version to it, so it ends in a slash or is made to.

columns.name: last_announced_at
columns.description: When this endpoint last announced itself over the DHT.

columns.name: verified_at
columns.description: When the public key behind this endpoint was last confirmed by asking it.

notes: This table was the original `communities`; migration 0065 renamed it and created a new communities table beside it. The two are still joined on public_key, which is why that column is the join key rather than a community id.

verified_at null with last_announced_at set is the normal state of a freshly discovered endpoint — announced but not yet asked. Both implementations must treat it as unverified rather than as an error.
Timestamps are UTC milliseconds; see types/Timestamp.json.
